title: SAML SSO for Cloud & Branch Connector admins: IdP-initiated sign-in, the break-glass super admin and the Okta, Azure AD and AD FS settings
aliases: cloud connector admin azure ad saml

prose.text: Cloud & Branch Connector admins can sign in with SAML initiated by an identity provider. {{idp-initiated}} {{no-auto-provisioning}} {{break-glass}}

prose.label: The entity ID.
prose.text: The two guides name different service provider entity IDs for the same sign-in URL {{divergence:sp-entity-id}}.

prose.label: Open.
prose.text: The console configuration step of each guide has no body in the capture {{gap:console-step}}, and whether the guides still apply on Authentication Service tenants is not stated {{gap:guides-current}}. Who may add admins is a role matter: [[shared.admin-rbac.cloud-connector:admin-mgmt]].

checks.do: Keep at least one super admin with password authentication so the console stays reachable if the SAML servers are unreachable.

idp-initiated.statement: The Zscaler service supports authenticating administrators using SAML initiated by an identity provider; an admin can log in to the Admin Console by single sign-on by clicking the Zscaler application icon in the provider's portal, and the service supports SAML 2.0 and later.

quotes: The Zscaler service supports authenticating administrators using SAML initiated by an identity provider (IdP).
An admin can log in to the Zscaler Admin Console directly via single sign-on (SSO) by clicking the Zscaler application icon within the provider's portal.
The Zscaler service supports SAML 2.0 and later.

no-auto-provisioning.statement: Admins are not added through auto-provisioning: an admin must be added in the Admin Console first and can then use SAML authentication to log in.

quotes: Admins are not added through auto-provisioning. Rather, you must add an admin in the Zscaler Admin Console, and then they can use SAML authentication to log in to it.

break-glass.statement: Zscaler recommends at least one super admin with password authentication enabled, so that an admin can still reach the Admin Console even if SAML servers external to the Zscaler service become unreachable.

quotes: Zscaler also recommends that you have at least one super admin with password authentication enabled to ensure that an admin can still access the Zscaler Admin Console even if SAML servers external to the Zscaler service become unreachable.

prerequisites.statement: The prerequisites are admin accounts for the organization's admins, a configured IdP (such as AD FS, Okta or Azure Active Directory) and the IdP's SAML certificate, which is uploaded to the Admin Console when configuring the service to use SAML.

quotes: Create admin accounts for your organization's admins.
Obtain the SAML certificate of the IdP. You upload this certificate to the Zscaler Admin Console when you configure the service to use SAML.
Configure an IdP, such as Active Directory Federation Services (AD FS), Okta, Azure Active Directory, etc.

zidentity-administration.statement: The configuration steps go to Administration > Legacy Admin Management > Branch and Cloud Connector > Administrators Management and say to click ZIdentity Administration to configure administrators.

quotes: From the navigation menu, go to Administration > Legacy Admin Management > Branch and Cloud Connector > Administrators Management.
Click ZIdentity Administration to configure your administrators.

auth-service-note.statement: The Okta, AD FS 3.0 and Azure AD admin SAML guides each say that if the organization is subscribed to Authentication Service, some of the options are configurable only within the Authentication Service Admin Portal.

quotes: If you are subscribed to Authentication Service, some of the following options are only configurable within the Authentication Service Admin Portal.
If you are subscribed to Authentication Service, some of the following options are only configurable within the Authentication Service Admin Portal.
If you are subscribed to Authentication Service, some of the following options are only configurable within the Authentication Service Admin Portal.

okta-acs.statement: In the Okta guide the Single sign on URL for the SAML settings is https://connector.<Zscaler Cloud>.net/bac-adminsso.do.

quotes: In SAML Settings, enter the following for Single sign on URL and Audience URI (SP Entity ID), respectively:
https://connector.<Zscaler Cloud>.net/bac-adminsso.do

okta-cert-format.statement: Okta downloads the certificate as a .cert, but the Admin Console supports only .cer or .pem files, so the file must be converted before uploading it.

quotes: Okta downloads the certificate as a .cert, but the Zscaler Admin Console supports only .cer or .pem files. Ensure that the file is converted before uploading it to the portal.

azure-reply.statement: In the Azure AD guide the Reply URL takes the form of the example https://connector.Zscalerbeta.net/bac-adminsso.do, with the Index field set to 1, and the optional Sign on URL is left blank.

quotes: Reply URL (Assertion Consumer Service URL): The Zscaler cloud name depends on the URL you use to log in to the Zscaler service.
For example, if you log in to https://connector.Zscalerbeta.net, then enter https://connector.Zscalerbeta.net/bac-adminsso.do. In the Index field, enter 1.
Sign on URL (Optional): Leave this field blank.

azure-assignment.statement: For Azure AD admins to authenticate through the Zscaler service, they must be assigned to the Zscaler Cloud and Branch Connector Administrator Application, which by default is visible to admins in their My Apps portal.

quotes: For Azure AD admins to authenticate through the Zscaler service, you must assign Azure AD admins to the Zscaler Cloud and Branch Connector Administrator Application.
By default, the Zscaler Cloud and Branch Connector Administrator Application is visible to admins in their My Apps portal.

adfs.statement: The AD FS guide is for a Windows Server 2012 R2 running AD FS 3.0 as the IdP; in it the LDAP attribute User-Principal-Name is mapped to the outgoing claim type Name ID, the certificate is exported as Base-64 encoded X.509 (.CER), and the IdP-initiated sign-in page is at https://<AD FS Server>/adfs/ls/idpinitiatedSignOn.aspx.

quotes: This guide demonstrates how to configure a Windows Server 2012 R2 running Active Directory Federation Services (AD FS) 3.0 as the identity provider (IdP)
Under Mapping of LDAP attributes to outgoing claim types, in LDAP Attribute, select User-Principal-Name.
Under Outgoing Claim Type, select Name ID, then click Finish.
In Export File Format, select Base-64 encoded X.509 (.CER), then click Next.
https://<AD FS Server>/adfs/ls/idpinitiatedSignOn.aspx

sp-entity-id.summary: The Okta guide gives admin.<Zscaler Cloud>.net as the service provider entity ID for Cloud & Branch Connector admin SAML; the Azure AD guide gives connector.<Zscaler Cloud>.net. Neither guide explains the difference.

quotes: In SAML Settings, enter the following for Single sign on URL and Audience URI (SP Entity ID), respectively:
admin.<Zscaler Cloud>.net

positions.says: Okta guide: the Audience URI (SP Entity ID) is admin.<Zscaler Cloud>.net.

quotes: Identifier (Entity ID): Enter connector.<Zscaler Cloud>.net as the identifier.

positions.says: Azure AD guide: the Identifier (Entity ID) is connector.<Zscaler Cloud>.net.

sp-entity-id.impact: An IdP configured from the wrong guide may send an entity ID the Admin Console does not expect; the pages do not say which value is accepted, whether both are, or whether it depends on the IdP, so confirm against the tenant.

console-step.title: The Admin Console SAML configuration step of the IdP guides
console-step.detail: Step 3 of each IdP guide, configuring SAML Admin SSO in the Admin Console, has no body in the capture, and the SAML configuration page sends admins to ZIdentity Administration instead.

guides-current.title: Whether the Okta, Azure AD and AD FS guides still apply on Authentication Service tenants
guides-current.detail: Each guide says some options are configurable only in the Authentication Service Admin Portal for subscribed tenants and the SAML page points to ZIdentity Administration; no capture says which of the guide's values still apply there, and the entity ID values conflict.
